sections.subtitle: Kratka poslanica s porukama koje su se izgubile: poziv da se uzme papir i olovka
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Vladimir Grebenar poziva gledatelje da uzmu papir i olovku i zapišu ključne pojmove spasenja
sections.content:
Nakon molitve Milosrdnom Isusu i Gospine krunice, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** prelazi na tumačenje Svete riječi i čita odlomak iz **Poslanice Filipljanima**. Sveti Pavao u tom odlomku hvali Filipljane što su poslušni „ne samo kao ono za moje nazočnosti, nego mnogo više sada za moje nenazočnosti“. Poziva ih da „sa strahom i trepetom“ rade oko svoga spasenja te da sve čine „bez mrmljanja i oklijevanja“. Tako će biti „djeca Božja neporočna“ usred „poroda izopačena i lukava“ u kojem svijetle „kao svjetlila u svijetu“. Apostol spominje i „dan Kristov“, a završava pozivom na radost: „A tako i vi budite radosni i radujte se sa mnom.“

Grebenar naglašava da je riječ o sažetom tekstu koji nosi iznimno važne poruke. Zato upućuje neobičan poziv gledateljima i slušateljima: neka uzmu papir i olovku i zapišu nekoliko riječi koje su, kako kaže, **ključne za spasenje**.

Po njegovu mišljenju, ti se pojmovi danas „jako rijetko spominju“, iako bi se trebali spominjati često, kao što ih spominje sveti Pavao. Uzrok vidi u onome što naziva **„bljutavom vjerom“**: zbog nje se izgubila spoznaja o tome što je za spasenje bitno. Tumačenje zatim gradi „redom“, pojam po pojam.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz Pavlova poziva da kršćani rade oko svoga spasenja, žive besprijekorno i svijetle u svijetu vjerno sažima Fil 2,12–16. Tvrdnja da je danas za to kriva „bljutava vjera” može biti retorička kritika, ali iz navedenog biblijskog odlomka ne slijedi kao dokazana opća tvrdnja.
concerns: U tekstu nije potkrijepljena tvrdnja da se ključni pojmovi spasenja danas vrlo rijetko spominju niti da je uzrok tome „bljutava vjera”; to je pastoralna procjena, a ne zaključak samoga citiranog odlomka.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao ne poziva na samospasenje neovisno o Bogu: odmah nakon poziva da vjernici rade oko svoga spasenja kaže da Bog djeluje u njima i htijenjem i djelovanjem. Zato „strah i trepet” treba razumjeti kao ozbiljnost i poniznost pred Bogom, a ne kao poricanje milosti ili razlog za očajanje.

citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: The presentation of Paul's call for Christians to work out their salvation, live blamelessly, and shine in the world faithfully summarizes Phil 2:12–16. The claim that “bland faith” is to blame for this today may be rhetorical criticism, but it does not follow from the cited biblical passage as a proven general claim.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul does not call for self-salvation independent of God: immediately after calling believers to work out their salvation, he says that God is at work in them both to will and to work. Therefore, “fear and trembling” should be understood as seriousness and humility before God, and not as a denial of grace or a reason for despair.
concerns_en: The text does not support the claim that key concepts of salvation are very rarely mentioned today, nor that the cause of this is “bland faith”; this is a pastoral assessment, and not a conclusion of the cited passage itself.

sections.subtitle_en: A short epistle with messages that have been lost: invitation to take paper and pen
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Vladimir Grebenar invites viewers to take paper and pen and write down key concepts of salvation
sections.content_en:
After the prayer to Merciful Jesus and Our Lady's Rosary, host **Vladimir Grebenar** proceeds to the interpretation of the Holy Word and reads a passage from the **Epistle to the Philippians**. In that passage, Saint Paul praises the Philippians for being obedient “not only as in my presence, but much more now in my absence”. He invites them to work out their salvation “with fear and trembling” and to do everything “without murmuring and wavering”. In this way they will be “blameless children of God” in the midst of a “crooked and perverse generation” in which they shine “as lights in the world”. The apostle also mentions the “day of Christ”, and concludes with a call to joy: “And you also be glad and rejoice with me.”

Grebenar emphasizes that this is a concise text that carries exceptionally important messages. Therefore, he extends an unusual invitation to viewers and listeners: let them take paper and pen and write down a few words that are, as he says, **key to salvation**.

In his opinion, these concepts are “very rarely mentioned” today, even though they should be mentioned often, just as Saint Paul mentions them. He sees the cause in what he calls **“lukewarm faith”**: because of it, the realization of what is essential for salvation has been lost. He then builds the interpretation “in order”, concept by concept.

sections.subtitle: Prvi pojam: poslušnost Bogu, vezanost uz Isusa, a ne uz propovjednika
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava da se Filipljani nisu vezali uz svetog Pavla, nego uz Isusa
sections.content:
Prvi pojam koji Grebenar izdvaja jest **poslušnost**: poslušnost Riječi Božjoj i volji Božjoj. Takvu poslušnost poistovjećuje s **poniznošću**.

Posebnu pozornost posvećuje Pavlovoj tvrdnji da su Filipljani još poslušniji sada, kad on nije s njima, nego dok je bio među njima. U tome Grebenar prepoznaje znak istinske vjere. Filipljani se, objašnjava, nisu vezali uz svetog Pavla, nego uz Isusa. Pavao je bio tek **sredstvo u Božjim rukama** kojim su Filipljani došli do Isusa. Kad je otišao, oni su se uz Isusa vezali još više.

Zaključak je jasan: poslušnost Bogu dolazi na prvo mjesto. Kad je čovjek Bogu poslušan, ističe voditelj, sve počinje gledati „drugim očima“.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na poslušnosti Bogu, poniznosti i tome da kršćanin ne smije svoju vjeru svesti na privrženost propovjedniku uglavnom je u skladu s Pavlovim tekstom. Tumačenje Filipljana koji su vjerniji i u Pavlovoj odsutnosti dobro odgovara objašnjenju da se njihova poslušnost pokazuje kao čin učinjen poradi Boga, a ne samo iz obzira prema apostolu.
concerns: Poistovjećivanje poslušnosti i poniznosti može biti pojednostavljujuće ako se shvati kao da su to isti pojmovi; poniznost je stav koji treba pratiti kršćansku poslušnost, ali u odlomku se izričito navode i drugi plodovi vjernosti, poput života bez mrmljanja i besprijekornosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao ne pripisuje duhovni napredak samo ljudskom naporu: u istom odlomku povezuje ljudsku odgovornost s Božjim djelovanjem u vjerniku. Ivan Zlatousti Pavlovu napomenu o odsutnosti tumači tako da se vidi kako je poslušnost bila „poradi Boga”, a ne tek zbog Pavlove prisutnosti ili autoriteta.

citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on obedience to God, humility, and the fact that a Christian must not reduce their faith to attachment to a preacher is mostly in accordance with Paul's text. The interpretation of the Philippians being more faithful even in Paul's absence corresponds well to the explanation that their obedience is shown as an act done for the sake of God, and not merely out of regard for the apostle.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul does not attribute spiritual progress solely to human effort: in the same passage, he links human responsibility to God's action in the believer. John Chrysostom interprets Paul's note about absence in such a way that it shows obedience was “for the sake of God”, and not just because of Paul's presence or authority.
concerns_en: Equating obedience and humility can be oversimplifying if understood as if they were the same concepts; humility is an attitude that should accompany Christian obedience, but the passage explicitly cites other fruits of faithfulness as well, such as life without grumbling and blamelessness.

sections.subtitle_en: The first concept: obedience to God, attachment to Jesus and not to the preacher
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains that the Philippians did not attach themselves to Saint Paul, but to Jesus
sections.content_en:
The first concept that Grebenar singles out is **obedience**: obedience to the Word of God and the will of God. He equates such obedience with **humility**.

He devotes special attention to Paul's statement that the Philippians are even more obedient now, when he is not with them, than while he was among them. In this Grebenar recognizes a sign of true faith. The Philippians, he explains, did not attach themselves to Saint Paul, but to Jesus. Paul was merely **an instrument in God's hands** through which the Philippians came to Jesus. When he left, they attached themselves to Jesus even more.

The conclusion is clear: obedience to God comes first. When a person is obedient to God, the host points out, he begins to see everything “with different eyes”.

sections.subtitle: Strah i trepet: Grebenarovo svjedočanstvo o paklu i duhovne vježbe svetog Ignacija
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj svjedoči da mu je Gospodin u duhu pokazao pakao
sections.content:
Drugi pojam je **strah i trepet**. Grebenar oštro odgovara onima koji tvrde da se Boga ne treba bojati i da se ljude ne smije plašiti Bogom. Pita ih otvoreno je li strah Božji dar od Boga, od ljudi ili od neprijatelja. Podsjeća i na psalam: „Blago onima koji se Boga boje.“ Kad se čovjek boji Boga, objašnjava, neće ni psovati ni griješiti.

Raditi oko spasenja „sa strahom i trepetom“ za njega znači **biti svjestan da čovjek može propasti za cijelu vječnost**, uzalud se truditi i završiti u paklu. Tu tvrdnju potkrepljuje Isusovim riječima: „Bojte se onoga koji može baciti u pakao“, a ne onih koji mogu ubiti tijelo. Nakon smrti tijela, ističe, život se nastavlja, a pitanje je samo gdje: u vječnom životu ili u vječnoj smrti.

Grebenar se poziva na **duhovne vježbe svetog Ignacija**, točnije na petu vježbu. U njoj se razmatra grijeh, a jedna od završnih točaka je razmatranje o paklu, u kojem čovjek moli da mu Duh Sveti stvarno pokaže pakao. Voditelj zatim iznosi osobno svjedočanstvo: kaže da mu je Gospodin pokazao pakao, da je u njemu bio „u duhu“ i vidio kako izgleda. Opisuje ga kao nešto „strašno, prestrašno“ i priznaje da ga je to iskustvo promijenilo.

Preporučuje i molitvu za posebnu milost. Ako čovjek u napasti smrtnog grijeha nema dovoljno zahvalnosti ni ljubavi prema Bogu, neka ga barem **strah od muka paklenih** uzdrži od grijeha. Grebenar tu milost smatra izrazito korisnom: da nije takva, ne bi bila u vježbama svetog Ignacija, niti bi je, kako kaže, Gospa dala Ignaciju u **Manrezi u Španjolskoj**.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na strah Božji može čovjeka odvratiti od grijeha i da ga se može razmatrati u duhovnim vježbama svetog Ignacija uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkom predajom i Fil 2,12; strah je valjan poticaj obraćenju, premda nije najviši oblik ljubavi prema Bogu. Ipak, osobno iskustvo viđenja pakla ne treba prikazivati kao nauk Crkve ni kao nešto što ta vježba zahtijeva: Ignacije opisuje maštovito razmatranje i molbu za unutarnji doživljaj boli, a ne nužno izvanredno viđenje ili objavu.
concerns: Tumačenje da molitelj treba tražiti da mu Duh Sveti stvarno pokaže pakao može zamagliti razliku između ignacijanskog maštovitog razmatranja i privatnog mističnog iskustva; u tekstu vježbe traži se unutarnji osjećaj boli kako bi strah od grijeha pomogao, a ne obećava se viđenje pakla.
Strah od pakla jest legitiman, ali ne bi ga trebalo predstaviti kao dostatni cilj kršćanskog života: izvor razlikuje taj manje savršeni poticaj od ljubavi prema Bogu kao najvišeg ideala.

Tvrdnje da je Gospa Ignaciju dala tu milost u Manrezi i da se voditelju dogodilo viđenje pakla nisu potvrđene dostupnim izvorima; stoga ih valja prikazati kao osobno svjedočanstvo ili tvrdnju koja zahtijeva zasebnu provjeru, a ne kao utvrđeni nauk.
magisterium.enrichment: Ignacijeva vježba izričito traži milost da strah od muka pomogne čovjeku ne upasti u grijeh ako zaboravi ljubav prema Gospodinu; završetak vježbe uključuje zahvalnost Kristu i promišljanje o njegovu milosrđu. Katolička tradicija zato ne odbacuje strah od suda, ali ga razumije kao mogući početni poticaj obraćenju koji treba voditi prema ljubavi, a ne kao zamjenu za nju.

citations.document_author: Íñigo López de Oñaz y Loyola (Ignatius of Loyola)

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that the fear of God can turn man away from sin and that it can be meditated upon in the Spiritual Exercises of Saint Ignatius is mostly in accordance with Catholic tradition and Phil 2:12; fear is a valid incentive for conversion, although it is not the highest form of love for God. However, personal experience of a vision of hell should not be presented as a teaching of the Church nor as something required by that exercise: Ignatius describes imaginative meditation and asking for an interior feeling of pain, and not necessarily an extraordinary vision or revelation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ignatius' exercise explicitly asks for the grace that the fear of torments may help man not fall into sin if he forgets the love of the Lord; the conclusion of the exercise includes gratitude to Christ and reflection on his mercy. Catholic tradition therefore does not reject fear of judgment, but understands it as a possible initial incentive for conversion that should lead toward love, and not as a substitute for it.
concerns_en: The interpretation that the person praying should ask the Holy Spirit to really show him hell can blur the distinction between Ignatian imaginative meditation and private mystical experience; in the text of the exercise, an interior sense of pain is sought so that fear of sin helps, and a vision of hell is not promised.
Fear of hell is legitimate, but it should not be presented as a sufficient goal of Christian life: the source distinguishes this less perfect incentive from love for God as the highest ideal.

Claims that Our Lady granted that grace to Ignatius in Manresa and that a vision of hell happened to the host are not confirmed by available sources; therefore, they should be presented as personal testimony or a claim requiring separate verification, and not as established teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: Fear and trembling: Grebenar's testimony about hell and the spiritual exercises of Saint Ignatius
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host testifies that the Lord showed him hell in the spirit
sections.content_en:
The second concept is **fear and trembling**. Grebenar responds sharply to those who claim that one should not fear God and that people must not be frightened with God. He asks them openly whether the fear of God is a gift from God, from men, or from the enemy. He also recalls the psalm: “Blessed are those who fear God.” When a person fears God, he explains, he will neither swear nor sin.

To work out salvation “with fear and trembling” means for him **to be aware that a person can be lost for all eternity**, strive in vain, and end up in hell. He supports that assertion with Jesus' words: “Fear him who can cast into hell”, and not those who can kill the body. After the death of the body, he emphasizes, life continues, and the only question is where: in eternal life or in eternal death.

Grebenar refers to the **spiritual exercises of Saint Ignatius**, more specifically to the fifth exercise. In it sin is meditated upon, and one of the concluding points is meditation on hell, in which a person prays that the Holy Spirit would truly show him hell. The host then presents a personal testimony: he says that the Lord showed him hell, that he was in it “in the spirit” and saw what it looks like. He describes it as something “terrible, too terrible” and admits that this experience changed him.

He also recommends a prayer for a special grace. If in the temptation of mortal sin a person lacks sufficient gratitude or love toward God, let at least the **fear of the torments of hell** hold him back from sin. Grebenar considers that grace extremely beneficial: were it not so, it would not be in the exercises of Saint Ignatius, nor would, as he says, Our Lady have given it to Ignatius in **Manreza in Spain**.

> "Magisterium alignment:" In Catholic moral theology and the Council of Trent, imperfect contrition (attrition), arising from the fear of hell and its torments, is recognized as a gift of the Holy Spirit and a salutary impulse that refrains from sin and disposes the soul toward the sacrament of penance, even though perfect contrition motivated by love of God is the ideal.

sections.subtitle: Mrmljanje kao proklinjanje: zašto, prema voditelju, mladi odlaze iz Hrvatske i BiH
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači da je mrmljanje proklinjanje koje pada na dom i potomstvo
sections.content:
Treći pojam iz poslanice jest **„bez mrmljanja“**. Grebenar opisuje ljude koji danas neprestano gunđaju i kojima je uvijek netko drugi kriv: svećenik u selu, poslodavac, politika, muž, žena, „krivi svi“. Upozorava da je Bogu mrsko vidjeti nezadovoljne ljude koji mrmljaju. Podsjeća da su Židovi upravo zbog mrmljanja „propali u pustinji“ i na sebe navukli prokletstvo.

To zatim povezuje sa stanjem u domovini. Mnogi su, tvrdi, po **Hrvatskoj te Bosni i Hercegovini** mrmljali protiv vlastite zemlje, politike i države u kojoj žive, i na njih je palo prokletstvo: djeca su im otišla u drugu zemlju. Njegova je teza da je **mrmljanje proklinjanje**. Kad čovjek proklinje zemlju u kojoj živi, prokletstvo pada na njegov dom, pa taj dom u toj zemlji više nema potomstva. Djeca odlaze u Njemačku, Austriju, „u bijeli svijet“, gdje je, prema njemu, često još gore, pa ondje izgube i vjeru.

Grebenar tvrdi da je **većina mladih iz Hrvatske i BiH otišla zbog mrmljanja roditelja**, a ne zbog ekonomske situacije. Kao uzrok navodi mučno ozračje neprestanog proklinjanja: „Kakva je ovo država? Ništa ne valja. Sve propada, svi kradu, sve korumpirano.“ Mladi to slušaju i odlaze čim odrastu. Neki im roditelji pritom i sami savjetuju da odu jer „sve propada“. Posljedica je, upozorava voditelj, osamljena starost.

Poziva roditelje da takvo mrmljanje „slome u ime Isusovo“, da rade na povratku djece i da ih zamole za oprost riječima poput: „Oprosti, dijete moje, kćeri moja, sine, ono što sam ja tako govorio.“

magisterium.assessment: Upozorenje da mrmljanje može biti znak nezahvalnosti prema Bogu ima uporište u kršćanskom tumačenju Fil 2,14, no tvrdnja da je mrmljanje roditelja uzrok iseljavanja djece ili da na njihov dom zbog toga pada prokletstvo nije potkrijepljena katoličkim naukom ni dostupnim izvorima. Takva uzročnost i pripisivanje odgovornosti roditeljima značajno su pretjerani, osobito jer je iseljavanje složeno pitanje, a traženje boljih životnih uvjeta izrijekom je prepoznato kao pravo radnika.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je većina mladih iz Hrvatske i BiH otišla zbog mrmljanja roditelja, a ne zbog ekonomskih razloga, iznesena je kao činjenična i duhovna uzročnost bez potpore u dostupnim izvorima.
Tvrdnja da proklinjanje zemlje uzrokuje odlazak potomstva i osudu doma na bezdječnost pripisuje obiteljskim događajima određenu nadnaravnu kaznu bez prikazane biblijske ili crkvene osnove.

Ovakvo tumačenje može nepravedno opteretiti roditelje krivnjom za odluke odrasle djece i zanemariti gospodarske i društvene okolnosti; Ivan Pavao II. govori o pravu radnika da ode u potrazi za boljim uvjetima te ističe odgovornost onih koji oblikuju gospodarski poredak.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivan Zlatousti doista upozorava da mrmljanje može izražavati nezahvalnost prema Bogu, ali taj duhovni ukor sam po sebi ne dokazuje da mrmljanje uzrokuje iseljavanje ili obiteljske posljedice opisane u podcastu. Katoličko razmatranje migracije uključuje i bolne posljedice za obitelji i zajednice, ali priznaje da ljudi mogu tražiti bolje životne uvjete u drugoj zemlji te poziva na odgovornost za gospodarske prilike. Poziv roditeljima da se ispričaju za štetne riječi može biti razborit korak pomirenja, no treba ga odvojiti od neutemeljenog obećanja da će time djeca nužno povratiti vjeru ili se vratiti.

citations.document_title: 4 November 1982: Mass at the Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe, Madrid - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: The warning that grumbling can be a sign of ingratitude toward God is grounded in the Christian interpretation of Phil 2:14, but the claim that parents' grumbling is the cause of children's emigration or that a curse falls upon their home because of it is not supported by Catholic teaching or available sources. Such causality and attribution of responsibility to parents are significantly exaggerated, especially since emigration is a complex issue, and seeking better living conditions is explicitly recognized as a right of workers.
magisterium.enrichment_en: John Chrysostom indeed warns that grumbling can express ingratitude toward God, but that spiritual rebuke in itself does not prove that grumbling causes the emigration or family consequences described in the podcast. Catholic reflection on migration includes painful consequences for families and communities, but recognizes that people may seek better living conditions in another country and calls for responsibility for economic conditions. The call for parents to apologize for harmful words can be a prudent step of reconciliation, but it should be separated from the unfounded promise that children will thereby necessarily regain faith or return.
concerns_en: The claim that most young people from Croatia and BiH left because of parents' grumbling, and not because of economic reasons, is presented as factual and spiritual causality without support in available sources.

The claim that cursing the land causes the departure of offspring and the condemnation of the home to childlessness attributes a certain supernatural punishment to family events without a demonstrated biblical or ecclesial basis.

Such an interpretation can unfairly burden parents with guilt for adult children's decisions and ignore economic and social circumstances; John Paul II speaks of the worker's right to leave in search of better conditions and highlights the responsibility of those who shape the economic order.

sections.subtitle_en: Murmuring as cursing: why, according to the host, young people leave Croatia and BiH
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets that murmuring is cursing that falls upon the home and offspring
sections.content_en:
The third concept from the epistle is **“without murmuring”**. Grebenar describes people today who constantly grumble and for whom someone else is always to blame: the priest in the village, the employer, politics, husband, wife, “everyone is to blame”. He warns that it is abhorrent to God to see dissatisfied people who murmur. He recalls that the Jews, precisely because of murmuring, “perished in the wilderness” and brought a curse upon themselves.

He then connects this with the situation in the homeland. Many, he asserts, throughout **Hrvatska and Bosna i Hercegovina** have murmured against their own country, the politics, and the state in which they live, and a curse fell upon them: their children went to another country. His thesis is that **murmuring is cursing**. When a person curses the land in which he lives, the curse falls upon his home, so that home no longer has offspring in that land. Children leave for Njemačka, Austrija, “into the wide world”, where, according to him, it is often even worse, so they lose their faith there as well.

Grebenar claims that **the majority of youth from Hrvatska and BiH left because of the murmuring of their parents**, and not because of the economic situation. As a cause, he cites the painful atmosphere of constant cursing: “What kind of country is this? Nothing is good. Everything is ruined, everyone steals, everything is corrupt.” Young people listen to this and leave as soon as they grow up. Some parents at the same time advise them themselves to leave because “everything is ruined”. The consequence, the host warns, is a lonely old age.

He invites parents to “break such murmuring in the name of Jesus”, to work on the return of their children, and to ask their forgiveness with words like: “Forgive me, my child, my daughter, my son, for what I used to say like that.”

sections.subtitle: „Duh komunizma“ među europskom mladeži i mržnja prema poduzetništvu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o mladima u Francuskoj i Njemačkoj i o mržnji prema poduzetnicima
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim upozorava kamo mladi zapravo odlaze. Prema njegovim riječima, mladi u **Francuskoj** mrze vlastitu zemlju, pale i uništavaju. U **Njemačkoj** nose crvene zastave sa srpom i čekićem i uništavaju trgovine po **Frankfurtu**, a mrze privatne radnje i poduzetništvo.

Objašnjenje vidi u tome što ih je, kako kaže, **„zahvatio duh komunizma“**. Ono što se događa naziva „komunističkom revolucijom u Europi i svijetu“. Mržnja prema poduzetnicima, tumači, proizlazi iz toga što su ti mladi sami nesposobni preuzeti odgovornost za svoj život, pa mrze one koji to mogu.

Kao primjere ljudi koji preuzimaju odgovornost navodi:
- obitelji s djecom,
- poduzetnike,
- poštene radnike i menadžere koji odgovorno zarađuju za sebe i svoju obitelj i tako služe Gospodinu.

Zaključuje da dio nove generacije mladih, generacije Z, mrzi Boga i ljude koji Boga vole. Zato ponovno upozorava: **bez mrmljanja**, jer je mrmljanje proklinjanje i „strašan govor“.

magisterium.assessment: Osuda nasilja i razaranja može biti u skladu s kršćanskom odgovornošću, ali odlomak ne potkrepljuje široke tvrdnje o mladima u Francuskoj i Njemačkoj niti zaključak da njihovo ponašanje proizlazi iz nesposobnosti za odgovornost ili mržnje prema Bogu. Takvo uopćavanje i pripisivanje motiva zamagljuje potrebu za pravednim razlučivanjem i ne proizlazi iz katoličkog nauka.
concerns: Povezivanje mladih kao skupine s mržnjom prema vlastitoj zemlji, poduzetnicima i Bogu generalizira bez pokazane osnove; crkveni tekst o mladima u Europi bilježi različite teškoće, ali i iskrenu potragu za smislom, solidarnošću i predanjem.

Tvrdnja da mladi razaraju trgovine u Frankfurtu, nose komunističke simbole ili su zahvaćeni „duhom komunizma” nije potvrđena dostupnim izvorima; iz njih se zato ne može zaključiti ni da je riječ o „komunističkoj revoluciji”.

Povezivanje protivljenja poduzetnicima s osobnom nesposobnošću za odgovornost pripisuje protivnicima motiv bez dokaza. Katolički tekst o mladima upozorava da slogani i nasilne metode mogu izobličiti ljudsko i kršćansko svjedočanstvo, ali to ne opravdava široko osuđivanje cijele generacije.

Izraz da je mrmljanje „proklinjanje” zvuči kao šira tvrdnja od samog biblijskog poziva da se izbjegava mrmljanje; bez dodatnog konteksta nije jasno misli li se na svako negodovanje ili na grešno, nepovjerljivo prigovaranje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička kritika nasilja može se izreći jasno, a da se pritom ne svede različite mlade ljude ili društvene pritužbe na jednu ideologiju ili jedan navodni motiv. Pavao VI. upozorava da nasilje može izobličiti ljudsko i kršćansko lice borbe, dok Ivan Pavao II. istodobno poziva na razmatranje i teškoća i pozitivnih težnji mladih.

citations.document_title: To the Bishops of Eastern France on their "ad Limina" visit (December 5, 1977) - Speech
To participants at the Symposium of the Council of Presbyterial Commissions of Europe (April 10, 1986) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: Condemnation of violence and destruction can be in accordance with Christian responsibility, but the passage does not substantiate broad claims about young people in France and Germany nor the conclusion that their behavior stems from inability to take responsibility or hatred toward God. Such generalization and attribution of motives blurs the need for just discernment and does not derive from Catholic teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic criticism of violence can be stated clearly without reducing different young people or social grievances to one ideology or one alleged motive. Paul VI warns that violence can disfigure the human and Christian face of struggle, while John Paul II simultaneously calls for consideration of both the difficulties and positive aspirations of youth.
concerns_en: Linking young people as a group with hatred toward their own country, entrepreneurs, and God generalizes without a demonstrated basis; Church text on youth in Europe notes various difficulties, but also a sincere search for meaning, solidarity, and dedication.

The claim that youth destroy shops in Frankfurt, wear communist symbols, or are seized by the “spirit of communism” is not confirmed by available sources; from them it cannot be concluded that it is a “communist revolution”.

Linking opposition to entrepreneurs with personal inability to take responsibility attributes a motive to opponents without proof. Catholic text on youth warns that slogans and violent methods can disfigure human and Christian witness, but this does not justify broad condemnation of an entire generation.

The expression that grumbling is “cursing” sounds like a broader claim than the biblical call itself to avoid grumbling; without additional context, it is not clear whether every displeasure is meant or sinful, distrustful complaining.

sections.subtitle_en: “Spirit of communism” among European youth and hatred toward entrepreneurship
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about young people in France and Germany and about hatred toward entrepreneurs
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then warns where young people are actually going. According to his words, youth in **Francuska** hate their own country, burn, and destroy. In **Njemačka** they carry red flags with the sickle and hammer and destroy shops across **Frankfurt**, and they hate private shops and entrepreneurship.

He sees the explanation in the fact that, as he says, **“the spirit of communism has gripped them”**. What is happening he calls a “communist revolution in Europe and the world”. Hatred toward entrepreneurs, he interprets, stems from the fact that these young people themselves are incapable of taking responsibility for their lives, so they hate those who can.

As examples of people who take responsibility he mentions:
- families with children,
- entrepreneurs,
- honest workers and managers who responsibly earn for themselves and their family and thus serve the Lord.

He concludes that a part of the new generation of youth, Generation Z, hates God and the people who love God. Therefore, he warns again: **without murmuring**, because murmuring is cursing and “terrible speech”.

sections.subtitle: Bez oklijevanja: „viza za raj ili viza za pakao“ u 47. godini života
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o vlastitoj životnoj prekretnici i ulasku u treću fazu života
sections.content:
Četvrti pojam je **„bez oklijevanja“**. Grebenar kritizira tipična odgađanja služenja Bogu: „pa ću još malo vidjeti“, „imam neke poslove“, „vratit ću se iz dijaspore“, „nisam kuću završio, nisam kredit otplatio“. Poruka mu je jednoznačna: ako je Gospodin čovjeku dao da nešto čini i to se potvrdi, „nema tu više čekanja“.

Zatim rezimira dosadašnje pojmove koje gledatelji trebaju zapisati: **poslušnost, strah i trepet, bez mrmljanja, bez oklijevanja**.

Dodaje i pojam iz poslanice koji se, ističe, piše velikim slovom: **„dan Kristov“**, odnosno dan **posljednjeg suda**. Na to nadovezuje osobno svjedočanstvo. U 47. je godini i ulazi u „treću fazu života“, potpuno svjestan da je ono što slijedi za njega „viza za raj ili viza za pakao“. To navodi kao jedan od razloga zašto sada putuje od grada do grada s promocijom knjige i navještajem Riječi Božje: to mu, kaže, daje Gospodin.

Svoj izbor potkrepljuje evanđeoskim riječima: „Tražite najprije kraljevstvo Božje, sve ostalo će vam se nadodati“ te „Tko više voli oca ili majku… ženu i djecu nego mene, nije me dostojan.“ Kad Gospodin dade zadaću, treba je izvršiti „hitro, brzo, spremno“. Sve što se čini na zemlji, ističe Grebenar, mora se činiti s posljednjim sudom pred očima.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na traženju Božjega kraljevstva, prvenstvu Krista i ozbiljnosti posljednjeg suda uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkom vjerom, a poziv da se Božji poziv ne odgađa može biti opravdan kad je poziv razlučen. Ipak, formulacija o „vizi za raj ili vizi za pakao” može zvučati kao da je spasenje jednostavna, unaprijed procjenjiva životna bilanca, a retorika hitnosti ne smije zanemariti odgovornost prema obitelji i drugim dužnostima.
concerns: Isusove riječi o prvenstvu nad obiteljskim vezama ne znače prezir prema obitelji niti ukidanje obiteljskih obveza; nauk Crkve govori o prvenstvu Krista među svim vezama, ne o tome da su druge veze bezvrijedne.

Poziv na hitnost ne bi se smio primijeniti tako da se posao, dovršetak doma, otplata duga ili skrb za obitelj automatski proglase nevažnim izgovorima; dostupni izvori ne razlučuju Grebenarov konkretni osobni poziv ni njegove okolnosti.
Slika „vize” može stvoriti dojam da osoba već sada može sa sigurnošću odrediti svoju konačnu sudbinu. Katekizam naglašava odgovornost, obraćenje i budnost upravo zato što čovjek ne zna dan ni čas.

„Sve ostalo će vam se nadodati” ne treba razumjeti kao obećanje da će vjerno služenje Bogu nužno donijeti zemaljski uspjeh ili ukloniti teškoće; u navedenom crkvenom tekstu naglasak je na prvenstvu Božjega kraljevstva i vjernosti pozivu.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska budnost pred sudom znači živjeti u obraćenju i odgovorno koristiti slobodu, a ne nagađati o vlastitoj konačnoj presudi; Crkva povezuje ozbiljnost vječnog odredišta s trajnim pozivom na obraćenje. Kristovo prvenstvo također usmjerava, a ne poništava, obiteljske i društvene veze: različiti su pozivi, pa se konkretna zadaća treba razlučiti i živjeti vjerno.

citations.document_title: To the youth of Benevento (July 2, 1990) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on seeking the Kingdom of God, the primacy of Christ, and the seriousness of the last judgment is mostly aligned with the Catholic faith, and the call not to postpone God's call can be justified when the vocation is discerned. However, the formulation about a “visa for heaven or visa for hell” can sound as if salvation were a simple, pre-calculable life balance sheet, and the rhetoric of urgency must not neglect responsibility toward family and other duties.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian vigilance before judgment means living in conversion and using freedom responsibly, not speculating about one's own final verdict; the Church links the seriousness of eternal destination with an ongoing call to conversion. Christ's primacy also directs, rather than nullifies, family and social ties: vocations differ, so a concrete task should be discerned and lived faithfully.
concerns_en: Jesus' words on primacy over family ties do not mean contempt for family or abolition of family obligations; Church teaching speaks of the primacy of Christ among all ties, not that other ties are worthless.

The call to urgency should not be applied in such a way that work, completing a home, debt repayment, or caring for family are automatically declared irrelevant excuses; available sources do not discern Grebenar's concrete personal vocation or his circumstances.

The image of a “visa” can create the impression that a person can already determine their final destiny with certainty. The Catechism emphasizes responsibility, conversion, and vigilance precisely because man does not know the day nor the hour.

“All these things will be added to you” should not be understood as a promise that faithful service to God will necessarily bring earthly success or eliminate difficulties; in the cited Church text, the emphasis is on the primacy of the Kingdom of God and faithfulness to one's calling.

sections.subtitle_en: Without wavering: “visa for heaven or visa for hell” in the 47th year of life
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about his own life turning point and entering the third phase of life
sections.content_en:
The fourth concept is **“without wavering”**. Grebenar criticizes typical postponements of serving God: “well, I'll see a bit more”, “I have some business”, “I will return from the diaspora”, “I haven't finished the house, I haven't repaid the loan”. His message is unambiguous: if the Lord gave a person something to do and that is confirmed, “there is no more waiting”.

Then he summarizes the concepts so far that the viewers should write down: **obedience, fear and trembling, without murmuring, without wavering**.

He also adds a concept from the epistle that, he emphasizes, is capitalized: the **“day of Christ”**, that is, the day of **the final judgment**. To that he attaches a personal testimony. He is in his 47th year and is entering the “third phase of life”, fully aware that what follows is for him a “visa for heaven or visa for hell”. He cites this as one of the reasons why he is now traveling from town to town with a book promotion and proclamation of the Word of God: this, he says, the Lord gives him.

He supports his choice with the evangelical words: “Seek first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you” and “He who loves father or mother… wife and children more than me is not worthy of me.” When the Lord gives an assignment, it should be carried out “swiftly, quickly, readily”. Everything that is done on earth, Grebenar emphasizes, must be done with the final judgment before one's eyes.

sections.subtitle: Protiv propovijedanja „u rukavicama“: Isus jedini Spasitelj
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira „duh Asiza“ i ističe da je Isus jedini Spasitelj
sections.content:
Grebenar otvara i pitanje odgovornosti onih koji propovijedaju. Mnogi, kaže, ne žele govoriti o posljednjem sudu, pa ni oni koji su to dužni. Pravdaju se time da ljude ne treba plašiti. On upozorava da će takvi biti **odgovorni ako ljudi propadnu** jer im istinu nisu rekli kako treba, nego „uvijeno, blagoglagoljivo, u rukavicama“, kako se ne bi zamjerili svijetu.

Istinu, ističe, treba govoriti bez ublažavanja. To posebno odnosi na ono što naziva **„duhom Asiza“** i herezama koje se šire u odnosu prema drugim religijama. Upućuje gledatelje da pročitaju što je, prema njegovim riječima, Gospa dala don Stefanu Gobiju, kao i proroštvo o duhu Asiza, koje naziva zabludom.

Prema Grebenarovu tumačenju, papa Vojtila htio je druge religije pozvati na obraćenje i na vjeru u Isusa Krista. Nije im htio poručiti da sve religije zajedno grade priču o zajedničkom miru i da se „stapaju u mir i ljubav“. Kad se Kristova Crkva na taj način otvori drugim religijama, tvrdi voditelj, **obezvrjeđuje se križ**, jer je **Isus jedini Spasitelj**.

Argument zaključuje retoričkom slikom: kad bi još netko umro na križu, možda bi mu bilo dopušteno pisati „treći zavjet“. Takvoga, međutim, nema. Mnogi bi danas pisali treći zavjet, napominje, ali ne bi išli na križ kao Isus.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da je Isus Krist jedini Spasitelj i da Crkva treba naviještati spasenje u njemu usklađen je s katoličkim naukom. Ipak, prikaz „duha Asiza” kao relativizma ili stapanja religija nije usklađen s objašnjenjem svetoga Ivana Pavla II., koji je izričito rekao da susret u Asizu nije bio sinkretizam, nego molitva za mir uz poštovanje drugih i jasno svjedočenje Krista.
concerns: Tvrdnja da se Crkva u Asizu „otvorila” drugim religijama tako da se one stapaju u zajedničku vjeru ne odgovara papinu opisu događaja: sudionici su molili za mir, ali kršćani nisu prihvaćali tuđe vjerske formule, niti je papa odustao od tvrdnje da se spasenje nalazi samo u Kristu.

Katolički nauk odbacuje shvaćanje da su religije kao takve usporedni ili dopunski putovi spasenja, ali dopušta priznati da u njima postoje elementi istine i dobrote te da Bog djeluje u životima nekršćana. Zato kritika religijskog relativizma treba razlikovati relativizam od poštovanja i međureligijskog susreta.

Upozorenje na odgovornost propovjednika može biti legitimno, ali tvrdnja da će ljudi propasti upravo zato što im je istina bila izrečena „u rukavicama” izrečena je previše kategorično; priloženi izvori ne utvrđuju takvu pojedinačnu uzročnu presudu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tvrdnja da je Krist jedini Spasitelj znači da svako spasenje dolazi po njemu, a ne da se kršćani moraju odnositi s prijezirom prema pripadnicima drugih religija. Ivan Pavao II. istodobno je učio da Crkva naviješta spasenje u Kristu i da se drugim religijama može pristupiti s iskrenim poštovanjem i gorljivim svjedočenjem Krista; pritom je događaj u Asizu izričito opisao kao nesinkretistički.
magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that Jesus Christ is the only Savior and that the Church should proclaim salvation in him is aligned with Catholic teaching. However, depicting the “spirit of Assisi” as relativism or the merging of religions is not aligned with the explanation of Saint John Paul II, who explicitly stated that the meeting in Assisi was not syncretism, but prayer for peace with respect for others and a clear witness of Christ.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic claim that Christ is the only Savior means that all salvation comes through him, and not that Christians must treat members of other religions with contempt. John Paul II taught simultaneously that the Church proclaims salvation in Christ and that other religions can be approached with sincere respect and fervent witness of Christ; in doing so, he explicitly described the event in Assisi as non-syncretic.
concerns_en: The claim that the Church in Assisi “opened up” to other religions so that they merge into a common faith does not correspond to the Pope's description of the event: participants prayed for peace, but Christians did not accept others' religious formulas, nor did the Pope abandon the claim that salvation is found only in Christ.

Catholic teaching rejects the notion that religions as such are parallel or complementary paths of salvation, but allows recognizing that there are elements of truth and goodness in them and that God acts in the lives of non-Christians. Therefore, criticism of religious relativism should distinguish relativism from respect and interreligious encounter.

Warning about the responsibility of preachers can be legitimate, but the claim that people will perish precisely because the truth was told to them “with kid gloves” is stated too categorically; the attached sources do not establish such an individual causal verdict.

sections.subtitle_en: Against preaching “with kid gloves”: Jesus the only Savior
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes the “spirit of Assisi” and emphasizes that Jesus is the only Savior
sections.content_en:
Grebenar also opens the question of the responsibility of those who preach. Many, he says, do not want to speak about the final judgment, not even those who are obliged to do so. They justify themselves by saying that people should not be frightened. He warns that such persons will be **held responsible if people perish** because they did not tell them the truth properly, but rather “in a veiled, sweet-talking way, with kid gloves”, so as not to offend the world.

The truth, he emphasizes, must be spoken without watering down. This applies especially to what he calls the **“spirit of Assisi”** and the heresies that are spreading in relation to other religions. He directs viewers to read what, according to his words, Our Lady gave to Father Stefano Gobbi, as well as the prophecy about the spirit of Assisi, which he calls a delusion.

According to Grebenar's interpretation, Pope Wojtyła wanted to call other religions to conversion and to faith in Jesus Christ. He did not want to tell them that all religions together build a story of common peace and that they “merge into peace and love”. When the Church of Christ opens itself in that way to other religions, asserts the host, **the cross is devalued**, because **Jesus is the only Savior**.

He concludes the argument with a rhetorical image: if someone else were to die on the cross, perhaps he would be permitted to write a “third testament”. There is, however, no such person. Many today would write a third testament, he notes, but they would not go to the cross like Jesus.

sections.subtitle: Peti pojam: kršćanska radost i psalam „Gospodin mi je svjetlost i spasenje“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja pitanje je li gledatelj radostan kršćanin
sections.content:
Na kraju tumačenja poslanice Grebenar izdvaja posljednji pojam: **radost**. Sveti Pavao kaže: „Radujem se. Radujte se sa mnom.“ Voditelj gledateljima postavlja izravno pitanje: jesu li radosni kršćani i jesu li sretni u životu zbog Isusa i zbog milosti koja ih nosi?

Poziva ih da zapišu sve što je rekao i da se na temelju toga **preispitaju**.

Slijedi čitanje psalma: „Gospodin mi je svjetlost i spasenje. Koga da se bojim? Gospodin je štit života moga. Pred kim da strepim?“ Psalmist moli za samo jedno: da živi u domu Gospodnjem sve dane života svoga. Psalam završava pozivom: „U Gospodina se uzdaj, ojunači se, čvrsto neka bude srce tvoje.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na radost zbog Krista i milosti, na osobno preispitivanje te pouzdanje u Gospodina u skladu je s kršćanskom porukom i citiranim psalmom. Jedina potrebna nijansa jest da kršćanska radost nije isto što i stalni osjećaj sreće: može postojati i usred žalosti, kušnji i patnje.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska radost izvire iz Božje ljubavi, Kristova uskrsnuća i nade u buduću preobrazbu, a ne iz obećanja da će život uvijek biti lak ili emocionalno vedar. Crkveno učenje prepoznaje da se ta radost može mijenjati kroz različita životna razdoblja, ostajući kao pouzdanje da je čovjek ljubljen i nošen Bogom; zato pitanje za savjest može biti plodno ako ne postane mjerilo kojim se osuđuju oni koji prolaze kroz žalost ili teškoće.

citations.document_title: Apostolic Journey to Canada: Vespers with Bishops, Priests, Deacons, Consecrated persons, Seminarians and Pastoral workers in the Cathedral of Notre Dame (Québec, 28 July 2022)

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to joy because of Christ and grace, to personal examination of conscience, and trust in the Lord is in accordance with the Christian message and the cited psalm. The only necessary nuance is that Christian joy is not the same as a constant feeling of happiness: it can exist even in the midst of sorrow, trials, and suffering.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian joy springs from God's love, Christ's resurrection, and hope in future transformation, not from a promise that life will always be easy or emotionally cheerful. Church teaching recognizes that this joy can vary through different life periods, remaining as confidence that one is loved and sustained by God; therefore, an examination of conscience can be fruitful if it does not become a yardstick used to judge those going through sorrow or hardship.

sections.subtitle_en: Fifth concept: Christian joy and the psalm “The Lord is my light and my salvation”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the question whether the viewer is a joyful Christian
sections.content_en:
At the end of the interpretation of the epistle, Grebenar singles out the last concept: **joy**. Saint Paul says: “I rejoice. Rejoice with me.” The host asks the viewers a direct question: are they joyful Christians and are they happy in life because of Jesus and because of the grace that carries them?

He invites them to write down everything he said and to **examine themselves** on that basis.

There follows the reading of the psalm: “The Lord is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? The Lord is the shield of my life. Before whom shall I tremble?” The psalmist prays for only one thing: to dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of his life. The psalm ends with the call: “Wait for the Lord, be strong, and let your heart take courage.”

sections.subtitle: Što znači „mrziti“ oca i majku: prezreti ljudski obzir kad je riječ o vjeri
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači riječ „mrziti“ iz evanđelja kao prezir ljudskog obzira
sections.content:
Grebenar čita evanđelje dana o **uvjetima učeništva**: tko ne mrzi oca i majku, ženu i djecu, braću i sestre, pa i sam svoj život, ne može biti Isusov učenik. Isus zatim navodi dvije prispodobe. Prva je o čovjeku koji gradi kulu, a ne proračuna troškove, pa mu se smiju jer je počeo graditi, a nije dovršio. Druga je o kralju koji prije rata promisli može li s 10.000 vojnika dočekati onoga koji dolazi s 20.000. Odlomak završava rečenicom: „Ni jedan od vas koji se ne odrekne svega što posjeduje, ne može biti moj učenik.“

Voditelj ističe da je Isusa slijedilo silno mnoštvo, i to uglavnom zato da im riješi životne probleme. Isus se, međutim, okreće tom mnoštvu i postavlja **Božje kriterije**. Mjerilo, naglašava Grebenar, nije ono što govore drugi, nego ono što govori Isus.

Tešku riječ **„mrziti“** tumači kao poziv da se u srcu **prezre ljudski obzir**. Roditelje treba slušati u svemu, osim kad je riječ o Bogu. Kad su „Božja pitanja na stolu“, čovjek ih nije dužan slušati, nego treba slušati Boga. Isto vrijedi za supružnika i djecu: njihovo mišljenje o vjeri je nebitno ako nisu jači u vjeri i ako nisu „kanal milosti“.

Grebenar pravi i važnu iznimku. Kad roditelji žive vjeru i savjetuju dijete kako da bude bolje, takav je savjet „dragocjen“, a blago onima koji imaju takve roditelje. Ako pak koče rast u vjeri, ne treba ih slušati.

Zaključuje upozorenjem na **idolatriju**. Ako je nečije mišljenje važnije od Isusova, Isus čovjeku nije Bog, nego to postaju ti ljudi. Takav se čovjek, kaže, klanja izmišljenom bogu, a to nisu „ni roditelji, ni muž, ni žena, ni djeca“.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno naglašava da Krist ima prvenstvo pred obiteljskim vezama i da se Njegovu pozivu ne smije suprotstaviti ljudski pritisak; „mrziti” u Lk 14,26 ne znači prezirati ili povrijediti obitelj, nego ne voljeti je više od Krista. Ipak, tvrdnja da mišljenje supružnika ili djece o vjeri nije važno ako nisu jači u vjeri preširoka je i može zanemariti obveze ljubavi, poštovanja i uzajamnog razlučivanja.
concerns: „Prezreti ljudski obzir” može zvučati kao poziv na prezir prema članovima obitelji, premda se evanđeoska riječ o mržnji ne smije shvatiti kao prezir ili nasilje, nego kao radikalno prvenstvo Boga.

Mišljenje supružnika i djece ne postaje nebitno samo zato što su slabiji u vjeri ili nisu „kanal milosti”; odlomak opravdava neposluh kada obiteljski zahtjev stvarno priječi vjernost Bogu, ali ne opravdava opće odbacivanje obiteljskog savjeta.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko tumačenje čita Isusovu tešku izreku uz Mt 10,37: obiteljske veze važne su, ali nisu apsolutne, jer je prvi poziv kršćanina slijediti Krista. Pontifikalna biblijska komisija pojašnjava da se „mržnja” ne odnosi na prezir ili nasilje, nego na to da obiteljska privrženost ne smije uvjetovati punu vjernost Kraljevstvu; obiteljska ljubav i skrb mogu, naprotiv, biti način nasljedovanja Krista.

“What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology

magisterium.assessment_en: It correctly emphasizes that Christ takes precedence over family ties and that human pressure must not oppose His call; “to hate” in Lk 14:26 does not mean to despise or harm family, but not to love them more than Christ. However, the claim that the opinion of a spouse or children about faith does not matter if they are not stronger in faith is too broad and can overlook the obligations of love, respect, and mutual discernment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic interpretation reads Jesus' hard saying alongside Mt 10:37: family ties are important, but not absolute, because the Christian's first call is to follow Christ. The Pontifical Biblical Commission clarifies that “hatred” does not refer to contempt or violence, but to the fact that family attachment must not condition full fidelity to the Kingdom; family love and care can, on the contrary, be a way of following Christ.
concerns_en: “Despising human regard” can sound like a call to contempt toward family members, although the Gospel word about hate must not be understood as contempt or violence, but as the radical primacy of God.

The opinion of a spouse and children does not become irrelevant merely because they are weaker in faith or are not a “channel of grace”; the passage justifies disobedience when a family demand truly hinders fidelity to God, but does not justify a general dismissal of family counsel.

sections.subtitle_en: What it means to “hate” father and mother: despising human respect when it comes to faith
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the word “hate” from the Gospel as contempt for human respect
sections.content_en:
Grebenar reads the Gospel of the day about the **conditions of discipleship**: whoever does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, and even his own life, cannot be Jesus' disciple. Jesus then relates two parables. The first is about a man who builds a tower and does not calculate the costs, so they mock him because he began to build and was not able to finish. The second is about a king who, before war, considers whether he can with 10,000 soldiers meet the one who comes with 20,000. The passage concludes with the sentence: “So therefore, whoever of you does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be my disciple.”

The host emphasizes that a great multitude followed Jesus, mainly in order for Him to resolve their life problems. Jesus, however, turns to that multitude and sets **God's criteria**. The standard, Grebenar emphasizes, is not what others say, but what Jesus says.

He interprets the hard word **“hate”** as a call to **despise human respect** in the heart. One should obey parents in everything, except when it comes to God. When “God's matters are on the table”, a person is not obliged to obey them, but must obey God. The same applies to spouse and children: their opinion on faith is irrelevant if they are not stronger in faith and if they are not a “channel of grace”.

Grebenar also makes an important exception. When parents live the faith and advise the child on how to be better, such advice is “precious”, and blessed are those who have such parents. If, however, they hinder growth in faith, they should not be listened to.

He concludes with a warning about **idolatry**. If someone's opinion is more important than Jesus's, Jesus is not a person's God, but those people become that. Such a person, he says, worships an invented god, and that is “neither parents, nor husband, nor wife, nor children”.

sections.subtitle: Ne napola: imovina u službi kraljevstva i djeca bez razmaženosti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o imovini u službi kraljevstva Božjeg i o odgoju djece
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim povezuje nošenje križa s prispodobom o gradnji kule. Po njegovu tumačenju, Isus poručuje da onaj tko je odlučio ići za kraljevstvom Božjim mora ići **svim srcem i sve založiti**, a ne biti „napola“. Ne može se „malo služiti, malo ne služiti“ ni služiti Gospodinu uz stalnu brigu o novcu, imovini i svjetovnom uspjehu.

Ako čovjeku treba imovina, kaže voditelj, ona mora služiti **širenju kraljevstva Božjega na zemlji**. To vrijedi za kuću, dom, stan, pa i hotel. Imovina nema svrhu u tome da se zgrne novac kojim će se djeci osigurati „bolja budućnost“.

Na to nadovezuje oštru opasku o odgoju. Djeca kojima se sve osigura, upozorava, zastrane, a roditelji od njih stvore „invalide nesposobne za život“. Savjetuje da djeca rade i bore se sama: **okolnosti siromaštva**, tvrdi, najbolje su za njihov odgoj. Djeca koja sve dobiju i kad odrastu žele sve „bez truda i rada“.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na cjelovito nasljedovanje Krista i unutarnju odvojenost od bogatstva u skladu je s evanđeoskim zahtjevom, ali odlomak neopravdano pretvara tu duhovnu raspoloživost u pravilo da svaka imovina mora služiti isključivo širenju Kraljevstva i da je siromaštvo najbolje za odgoj. Takve kategorične tvrdnje nisu potvrđene navedenim naukom i osobito su problematične jer prikazuju materijalnu oskudicu kao općenito poželjan odgojni uvjet.
concerns: Katolici su pozvani na siromaštvo duha, odvojenost od dóbara i velikodušno dijeljenje, ali konkretan opseg odricanja ovisi o životnom stanju i pozivu; iz evanđeoskog poziva ne slijedi da svaki kršćanin mora svu imovinu upotrijebiti samo za izravno širenje Kraljevstva.

Tvrdnja da su okolnosti siromaštva najbolje za odgoj djece pretjerano je generalizirana. Siromaštvo može ozbiljno opteretiti obitelj i oslabiti obiteljske veze, pa ga ne treba predstavljati kao poželjan odgojni ideal.
Oprez prema ugađanju djeci i materijalizmu može biti razborit, ali ne opravdava zanemarivanje roditeljske odgovornosti da se skrbi za djecu i njihovu budućnost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katekizam uči da učenik treba biti spreman odreći se svega radi Krista, a crkveni nauk pritom razlikuje opću obvezu unutarnje odvojenosti od imovine od konkretnog načina života koji se prilagođuje pozivu i okolnostima. Kršćansko upravljanje dobrima traži da ona ne postanu idol te da se dijele velikodušno, ali ne svodi njihovu svrhu na jednu formulu za sve obitelji. Papa Franjo upozorava da materijalna oskudica može teško raniti obiteljski život, što je u napetosti s tvrdnjom da su okolnosti siromaštva najbolje za odgoj.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 3 June 2015: The family - 17. Family and poverty

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to integral following of Christ and interior detachment from riches is in accordance with the Gospel requirement, but the passage unjustifiably turns that spiritual availability into a rule that all property must serve exclusively the expansion of the Kingdom and that poverty is best for upbringing. Such categorical claims are not confirmed by the stated teaching and are especially problematic because they depict material deprivation as a generally desirable condition for upbringing.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catechism teaches that a disciple should be ready to renounce everything for Christ, and Church teaching thereby distinguishes the general obligation of interior detachment from possessions from a concrete way of life adapted to one's vocation and circumstances. Christian stewardship of goods requires that they do not become an idol and that they be shared generously, but does not reduce their purpose to a single formula for all families. Pope Francis warns that material deprivation can gravely wound family life, which stands in tension with the claim that circumstances of poverty are best for upbringing.
concerns_en: Catholics are called to poverty of spirit, detachment from goods, and generous sharing, but the concrete scope of renunciation depends on one's state of life and vocation; it does not follow from the evangelical call that every Christian must use all property solely for the direct expansion of the Kingdom.

The claim that circumstances of poverty are best for raising children is overly generalized. Poverty can seriously burden a family and weaken family bonds, so it should not be presented as a desirable educational ideal.
Caution toward indulging children and materialism may be prudent, but it does not justify neglecting parental responsibility to provide for children and their future.

sections.subtitle_en: Not halfway: property in the service of the kingdom and children without pampering
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about property in the service of the kingdom of God and about raising children
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then connects carrying the cross with the parable of building the tower. According to his interpretation, Jesus conveys that whoever has decided to follow the kingdom of God must go **with all his heart and wager everything**, and not be “halfway”. One cannot “serve a little, not serve a little” nor serve the Lord with constant worry about money, property, and worldly success.

If a person needs property, says the host, it must serve the **spreading of the kingdom of God on earth**. That applies to a house, a home, an apartment, and even a hotel. Property does not have its purpose in amassing money with which to secure a “better future” for children.

To this he attaches a sharp remark about upbringing. Children for whom everything is secured, he warns, go astray, and parents create from them “invalids unfit for life”. He advises that children work and fight on their own: **circumstances of poverty**, he asserts, are best for their upbringing. Children who receive everything, even when they grow up, want everything “without effort and work”.

sections.subtitle: Dom kao „mala crkva“: velika obitelj i primjeren životni prostor
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj navodi primjer stana od 150 kvadrata u kojem živi tročlana obitelj
sections.content:
Sve treba podrediti kraljevstvu Božjem, nastavlja Grebenar, pa i vlastitu kuću i stan. Ako treba seliti, treba seliti, jer će Bog dati kuću i stan. Svrha doma, kaže, jest da ga se **napuni djecom** i da postane **„mala crkva“**.

Velik dom u kojem živi velika obitelj za njega je „prava stvar“ kojoj se nema što prigovoriti. Obitelj s četvero, petero ili desetero djece ne može živjeti na 40 kvadrata i treba joj veći prostor. Takav je dom „crkva u malom“.

Drukčije je, upozorava, kad tročlana obitelj živi na 150 kvadrata: tada „nešto ne štima“. Predlaže konkretno rješenje: prodati takav stan, kupiti primjeren stan od 60 kvadrata, a ostatak uložiti u nešto drugo, primjerice:
- pokrenuti posao i zaposliti ljude,
- dati Crkvi,
- dati inicijativi.

Sažetak njegove poruke glasi: treba se odreći imovine koja nije potrebna, zadržati dovoljno, a višak „upregnuti“ u širenje kraljevstva Božjega. Tko zna kako, neka to učini sam. Tko ne zna, neka da nekome tko zna.

Tumačenje zaključuje podsjetnikom da je vrijeme kratko i da na spasenju treba raditi „sa strahom i trepetom“. Prema Isusovim riječima, nitko tko se ne odrekne svega što posjeduje ne može biti njegov učenik. Zato treba biti spreman izgubiti sve. Ono što čovjeku ne treba, kaže Grebenar, treba prodati ili darovati „na slavu Božju“, kako Duh Sveti nadahne.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na velikodušnosti, usmjerenosti prema Božjem kraljevstvu i obitelji kao „kućnoj Crkvi“ može biti u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem doma i kršćanskoga života. Ipak, tvrdnje da je svrha doma da se napuni djecom te da je velika kuća za tročlanu obitelj znak da „nešto ne štima“ mogu nametati neosnovan sud i preusko prikazati obiteljsku i imovinsku odgovornost.
concerns: Katoličko razumijevanje obitelji kao kućne Crkve odnosi se na njezin život vjere, molitve, zajedništva i ljubavi, a ne na određenu veličinu obitelji ili doma; obiteljski dom može postati kućna Crkva kao mjesto zajedničke molitve i Kristove prisutnosti.

Izlaganje ne razlikuje dovoljno evanđeoski poziv na odricanje i slobodu od navezanosti na imetak od univerzalne obveze da se proda višak imovine. Prijedlog darivanja Crkvi ili inicijativi može biti slobodan čin velikodušnosti, ali odlomak ne daje osnovu da se određena kvadratura ili darivanje konkretnoj inicijativi proglasi mjerilom vjernosti.

Procjena da je dom od 150 kvadrata za tročlanu obitelj znak da „nešto ne štima“ iznosi se bez razmatranja okolnosti, potreba i odgovornosti te obitelji. Takav sud može nepotrebno poistovjetiti kršćansko siromaštvo ili velikodušnost s jednim propisanim životnim standardom.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk opisuje obiteljski dom kao mjesto prvoga navještaja vjere te kao zajednicu milosti i molitve, školu kreposti i kršćanske ljubavi; pojam „kućne Crkve“ zato prije svega govori o načinu života, a ne o površini doma. Velikodušno raspolaganje imovinom može biti način služenja Bogu i bližnjima, ali obiteljske odluke o domu i darivanju treba prosuđivati razborito, uzimajući u obzir stvarne potrebe i dužnosti obitelji.
magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on generosity, orientation toward the Kingdom of God, and the family as the “domestic church” can be in accordance with the Catholic understanding of home and Christian life. However, claims that the purpose of a home is to be filled with children and that a large house for a family of three is a sign that “something is not right” can impose an unfounded judgment and portray family and property responsibility too narrowly.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching describes the family home as the place of the first proclamation of the faith and as a community of grace and prayer, a school of virtues and Christian love; the concept of the “domestic church” therefore primarily speaks of a way of life, and not of the square footage of the home. Generous disposal of property can be a way of serving God and neighbors, but family decisions about the home and giving should be judged prudently, taking into account the real needs and duties of the family.
concerns_en: The Catholic understanding of the family as the domestic church refers to its life of faith, prayer, communion, and love, and not to a specific size of the family or home; the family home can become a domestic church as a place of common prayer and Christ's presence.

The exposition does not sufficiently distinguish the evangelical call to renunciation and freedom from attachment to possessions from a universal obligation to sell excess property. A proposal to donate to the Church or an initiative can be a free act of generosity, but the passage provides no basis for declaring a specific square footage or donating to a concrete initiative as a standard of faithfulness.

The assessment that a 150-square-meter home for a family of three is a sign that “something is not right” is stated without considering the circumstances, needs, and responsibilities of that family. Such a judgment can unnecessarily equate Christian poverty or generosity with a single prescribed standard of living.

sections.subtitle_en: Home as a “little church”: large family and adequate living space
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host cites the example of a 150-square-meter apartment where a three-member family lives
sections.content_en:
Everything should be subordinated to the kingdom of God, Grebenar continues, even one's own house and apartment. If one needs to move, one should move, because God will provide a house and apartment. The purpose of a home, he says, is to **fill it with children** and for it to become a **“little church”**.

A large home where a large family lives is for him “the real thing” to which there is nothing to object. A family with four, five, or ten children cannot live in 40 square meters and needs a larger space. Such a home is a “church in miniature”.

It is different, he warns, when a family of three lives in 150 square meters: then “something is not right”. He proposes a concrete solution: sell such an apartment, buy an adequate apartment of 60 square meters, and invest the rest in something else, for example:
- start a business and employ people,
- give to the Church,
- give to the initiative.

The summary of his message is: one should renounce property that is not needed, keep enough, and “harness” the surplus into the spreading of the kingdom of God. Whoever knows how, let him do it himself. Whoever does not know, let him give to someone who knows.

He concludes the interpretation with a reminder that time is short and that one must work out salvation “with fear and trembling”. According to Jesus' words, no one who does not renounce all that he possesses can be His disciple. Therefore, one should be ready to lose everything. What a person does not need, says Grebenar, should be sold or donated “for the glory of God”, as the Holy Spirit inspires.

sections.subtitle: Promocije knjige od Imotskog do Samobora: Umag umjesto Buja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje raspored promocija knjige i promjenu lokacije iz Buja u Umag
sections.content:
Nakon tumačenja Grebenar najavljuje predstavljanja knjige i domoljubne inicijative u nadolazećim danima. Gledatelje iz pojedinih krajeva moli da najave podijele na društvenim mrežama i pozovu one kojima je, kako kaže, potrebno čuti Riječ Božju.

- **Petak, 6. studenoga – Pazin**, hotel Lovac. Voditelj napominje da se istodobno održava duhovna obnova koja će trajati nešto kraće. Najavljuje da će možda pomaknuti krunicu kako bi sudionici obnove stigli i na promociju u hotelu, oko 20 sati.
- **Subota, 7. studenoga – Umag**, hotel Garden Istra, Katoro 19

Posebno naglašava **promjenu lokacije**: susret se ne održava u Bujama, kako je dan ranije rečeno i objavljeno na Facebook stranici, nego u **Umagu**. Zahvaljuje bratu koji mu je pomogao pronaći dvoranu. Kako ne bi bilo zabune, više puta ponavlja: „Ne Buje, već Umag.“ Gledatelje iz Umaga i okolice moli da s Facebook stranice preuzmu banner i podijele ga.

**Sljedeći tjedan:**
- **Utorak, 10. studenoga – Valpovo**, Vila Valpovo, Bana Josipa Jelačića 1
- **Srijeda, 11. studenoga – Nova Gradiška**, Centar kompetencija
- **Četvrtak, 12. studenoga – Bjelovar**, Tehnološki park

magisterium.assessment: Najave predstavljanja knjige i inicijative te poziv da se informacija podijeli s ljudima kojima bi koristilo čuti Božju riječ sami po sebi ne iznose tvrdnju koja bi bila u sukobu s katoličkim naukom. Odlomak je pretežno informativan, pa iz njega se ne može procijeniti ni sadržaj događanja ni vjernost knjige ili inicijative nauku Crkve.
magisterium.enrichment: Poziv na slušanje Božje riječi može se razumjeti kao poticanje na upoznavanje vjere, ali teološka vrijednost susreta ovisi i o sadržaju koji se ondje iznosi. Katoličko poimanje doma i obitelji naglašava da se vjera ne prenosi samo riječima nego i zajedničkom molitvom, životom ljubavi i djelima kršćanske ljubavi.
magisterium.assessment_en: Announcements of book presentations and the initiative, along with the invitation to share information with people who would benefit from hearing the word of God, do not in themselves make a claim that would conflict with Catholic teaching. The passage is predominantly informative, so neither the content of the events nor the fidelity of the book or initiative to Church teaching can be assessed from it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: An invitation to hear the word of God can be understood as encouraging knowledge of the faith, but the theological value of the meeting also depends on the content presented there. The Catholic concept of home and family emphasizes that faith is transmitted not only by words but also by common prayer, a life of love, and works of Christian charity.

sections.subtitle: Poziv na članstvo, svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju i pomoć centru u Međugorju
sections.screenshot_description: Na ekranu podaci za uplatu donacija dok voditelj čita svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju od nesanice
sections.content:
Grebenar poziva sve gledatelje da preko web forme postanu članovi **domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora**. Na ekranu su brojevi mobitela za Hrvatsku te Bosnu i Hercegovinu. Onima koji odustanu jer im prijava „ne prolazi“ savjetuje da ne odustaju, nego da nazovu navedene kontakte i pitaju.

Zahvaljuje svima koji pomažu i poziva na donacije: neka gledatelji budu „široke ruke i otvorena srca“. Ističe da inicijativa zna što će s prikupljenim sredstvima.

Čita i svjedočanstvo jedne gledateljice. Zahvalna je Gospodinu za **petodnevni post o kruhu i vodi** nakon kojeg je, kako svjedoči, **ozdravila od nesanice nakon punih osam godina nespavanja**. Ostale potiče da se pridruže molitvi i postu.

Slijedi poziv na **molitvu krunice po hrvatskim gradovima** u subotu. Za vjernike iz dijaspore, iz Njemačke i Austrije, organiziran je prijevoz do zagrebačkog glavnog trga, a kontakt-brojevi prikazani su na ekranu. Voditelj završava blagoslovom: „Neka se sveta Mati sa svojim Sinom i svetim Josipom udostoji blagoslov svoj nam dati.“

Na samom kraju upućuje osobnu molbu. Poziva gledatelje da kupe prvu, drugu i treću knjigu **„Isus lider“** i tako mu pomognu dovršiti **međunarodni edukacijski centar Kraljica Mira u Međugorju**. Naglašava da mu je baš ovih dana potrebno da projekt završi, i financijski, te i tu nakanu povjerava molitvi gledatelja. Zahvaljuje svima koji su knjige već kupili i poziva da svaki dan prate Ora et Labora, „na veću slavu Božju“.

magisterium.assessment: Pozivi na molitvu, krunicu, post i darivanje mogu biti u skladu s katoličkom pobožnošću, a povjerenje u zagovor Marije i svetoga Josipa samo po sebi nije sporno. Ipak, odlomak ostavlja važne nejasnoće: petodnevni post povezuje se s ozdravljenjem bez dodatne provjere ili opreza, a financijski poziv za osobni projekt traži veću transparentnost.
concerns: Svjedočanstvo o nestanku nesanice nakon posta prenosi se kao vremenski slijed, ali može se shvatiti kao dokaz da je post uzrokovao ozdravljenje. Crkvena uputa za službe ozdravljenja traži da se svjedočanstva prikupljaju pošteno i točno te podnesu nadležnoj crkvenoj vlasti; u ovom odlomku ne spominje se takva provjera.

Poziv slušateljima da se pridruže petodnevnom postu o kruhu i vodi ne uključuje upozorenje da se post mora provoditi razborito i u skladu sa zdravstvenim mogućnostima. Post je kršćanska vježba, ali nije sam po sebi jamstvo ozdravljenja niti bi trebalo sugerirati da je određeni oblik posta prikladan za sve.

Traženje donacija i kupnje knjiga radi dovršetka centra nije samo po sebi neprikladno, no spajanje duhovnog poziva s osobnom financijskom potrebom može stvoriti pritisak. Za povjerenje darovatelja bilo bi važno jasno prikazati namjenu, upravljanje i uporabu sredstava; transkript ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se procijenilo kako se njima postupa.
magisterium.enrichment: Isus uči da se post i milostinja trebaju vršiti pred Bogom, a ne radi priznanja ili pritiska na druge; to ne zabranjuje javni poziv na molitvu ili darivanje, nego traži iskrenu nakanu i slobodan odgovor. Kršćanski post usmjeren je obraćenju, samodisciplini i ljubavi prema bližnjemu, a ne samoj tjelesnoj oskudici ili obećanju određenog ishoda.

Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: Calls to prayer, the Rosary, fasting, and giving can be in accordance with Catholic devotion, and trust in the intercession of Mary and Saint Joseph is not in itself disputed. However, the passage leaves important ambiguities: a five-day fast is linked to healing without additional verification or caution, and the financial appeal for a personal project requires greater transparency.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus teaches that fasting and almsgiving should be performed before God, and not for recognition or pressure on others; this does not prohibit a public call to prayer or giving, but requires sincere intention and a free response. Christian fasting is directed toward conversion, self-discipline, and love of neighbor, and not to bodily deprivation alone or the promise of a specific outcome.
concerns_en: The testimony about the disappearance of insomnia after fasting is conveyed as a temporal sequence, but it can be understood as proof that fasting caused healing. The Church's instruction for healing ministries requires that testimonies be collected honestly and accurately and submitted to the competent Church authority; this passage makes no mention of such verification.

The invitation to listeners to join a five-day fast on bread and water does not include a warning that fasting must be undertaken prudently and in accordance with health capabilities. Fasting is a Christian exercise, but it is not in itself a guarantee of healing, nor should it be suggested that a specific form of fasting is appropriate for everyone.

Requesting donations and book purchases to complete the center is not in itself inappropriate, but combining a spiritual call with a personal financial need can create pressure. For donors' trust, it would be important to clearly present the purpose, governance, and use of funds; the transcript does not provide enough data to assess how they are handled.

sections.subtitle_en: Call to membership, testimony of healing, and assistance to the center in Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: On the screen are donation payment details while the host reads a testimony of healing from insomnia
sections.content_en:
Grebenar invites all viewers to become members of the **patriotic initiative Ora et Labora** via the web form. On the screen are mobile phone numbers for Hrvatska and Bosna i Hercegovina. To those who give up because their registration “does not go through”, he advises not to give up, but to call the indicated contacts and ask.

He thanks all who are helping and calls for donations: let viewers be “of generous hand and open heart”. He points out that the initiative knows what to do with the collected funds.

He also reads the testimony of a female viewer. She is grateful to the Lord for a **five-day fast on bread and water** after which, as she testifies, **she was healed of insomnia after full eight years of sleeplessness**. He encourages others to join in prayer and fasting.

There follows a call to the **recitation of the rosary across Croatian cities** on Saturday. For faithful from the diaspora, from Njemačka and Austrija, transportation to the main square in Zagreb is organized, and contact numbers are displayed on the screen. The host ends with a blessing: “May the holy Mother with her Son and Saint Joseph deign to bestow their blessing upon us.”

At the very end, he makes a personal appeal. He invites viewers to buy the first, second, and third books **“Isus lider”** and thus help him complete the **international educational center Kraljica Mira in Međugorje**. He emphasizes that it is precisely these days that he needs the project to be completed, including financially, and he entrusts that intention as well to the prayer of the viewers. He thanks all who have already bought the books and invites them to follow Ora et Labora every day, “for the greater glory of God”.
